newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says China silenced dissent, faults others.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says China silenced dissent, faults others.

text.p: The United States on Thursday accused China of effectively silencing all public dissent against the communist party and government in 1996.

In its annual human rights report of 193 countries, being issued for the 20th year, the State Department also found problems with the rights records of allies Turkey, South Korea and Germany as well as Russia, Indonesia, Haiti, Nigeria and countries on the U.S. terrorism list including Cuba, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Syria and North Korea.

Its findings on China were of especially wide interest because of U.S. efforts to build a better working relationship with the communist giant, and the conclusion was that "no dissidents were known to be active (in China) at year's end."

"The Chinese government in 1996 continued to commit widespread and well-documented human rights abuses, in violation of internationally-accepted norms, stemming from the authorities' intolerance of dissent, fear of unrest and the continuing absence of laws protecting basic freedoms," it said.
"All public dissent against party and government was effectively silenced by intimidation, exile or the imposition of prison terms, administrative detention or house arrest."
The United States regularly criticises China's record in its annual assessment of human rights around the world.
But this year's hard-hitting report comes as Washington and Beijing were making a major effort to improve their relationship, which had deteriorated seriously.
The report's conclusion would seem to make it impossible for the United States not to sponsor a controversial resolution at the Human Rights Commission in Geneva faulting China's record.

In fact, U.S. officials have told Reuters they expect the Clinton administration to proceed with the resolution in conjunction with European allies. But they acknowledge such a resolution is unlikely to be adopted.

New Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has said she will pursue a policy of inclusion rather than isolation towards China and, while keen to foster human rights, does not want to hold the overall relationship hostage to one issue.
The report said Turkey had serious human rights problems in 1996 and its record deteriorated in some respects.

"The (Turkish) government was unable to sustain improvements made in 1995 and, as a result, its record was uneven in 1996 and deteriorated in some respects," it said, adding: "Serious human rights problems continued."

The section on South Korea said violence against women, especially rape, is a serious problem there. "Women continued to face legal and societal discrimination. Violence against women and physical abuse remain serious problems," it said.

The Afghanistan review contained what may be the toughest U.S. criticism of the Moslem group that has taken over much of the country, saying, "discrimination (against women) reached new heights of severity in Afghanistan with the rise to power of the Taliban."
It said Russia's rights record showed little progress last year, with Russian forces using "indiscriminate and disproportionate" force in the breakaway Republic of Chechnya.

The department, as expected, took issue with Germany for discriminating against Scientology in business and cultural life, but said there had also been "some positive developments" in Bonn's treatment of the group.

It found Indonesia continued to commit serious human rights abuses in 1996, including in East Timor. "While Indonesia exhibits a surface adherence to democractic firms, its political system remains strongly authoritarian," it said.

The report said political killings in Haiti rose last year from 1995, but remained far fewer than in the years that led to the U.S. military operation that restored the first democratically elected president.
In the Middle East, it said Israel's withdrawal from the West Bank led to improved human rights but both Israel and the Palestinian Authority continue to commit serious abuses.
The human rights record of communist-ruled Cuba worsened last year with a crackdown on a pro-democracy umbrella group and many other alleged abuses of power, the report said.
It said Nigeria's human rights performance remains dismal.

On the positive side, the department asserted that a broad consensus has been steadily emerging against fundamental rights abuses. "Even those who engage in these practices rarely seek to justify their actions outright," it said.
